transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-07 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jon Park (Redwood SE), Serena Li (Redwood CSM), Carlos Ruiz (Nimbus CTO), Aisha Khan (Platform Eng), Ben Cho (Security), Lina Torres (PM)

Summary (auto): Discussed rollout plan for POC -> production cutover, canary strategy (5% -> 25%), monitoring and runbooks, rollback criteria, security sign-offs, next steps and responsibilities.

00:00 Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick check, can you all hear me?
00:04 Carlos Ruiz: Yep, loud and clear.
00:06 Maya Patel: Great. So agenda today, we want to lock down the cutover/canary approach, confirm monitoring and runbook ownership, and align on timelines so we can target mid-Jan go-live window.
00:18 Jon Park: I'll walk through the proposed canary topology and the metrics we'll be watching - latency, error rates, token costs, and quality regressions on our eval set.
00:27 Aisha Khan: Quick context — we've got about 200 RPS peak for our auth routes, most of the validation traffic will be in a handful of routes. We're planning to send a 5% sample for the canary initially.
00:40 Maya Patel: OK, 5% sounds reasonable. Do you have a list of the top routes?
00:44 Aisha Khan: Not yet, we'll share the top 20 by end of day Friday, that's in the action items.
00:50 Jon Park: For the canary flow, Redwood will route chosen traffic to the dedicated pilot pool (dedicated capacity on our side) and we'll keep a mirrored stream to your current production model for comparison; we'll capture p95/p99 latencies, token cost delta, and output diffs.
01:05 Ben Cho: On security — we need to validate KMS key management, SSO integration (SAML), and ensure audit logs are streaming to our SIEM. Also SOC2 attestation docs; we did get the doc set but want the specific retention window for logs.
01:18 Maya Patel: Understood. We'll push the KMS architecture doc and audit log retention policies. Note: on private deployments we support customer-managed KMS, and for hosted we use Redwood KMS with envelope encryption.
01:30 Ben Cho: Can you confirm that the KV cache won't persist sensitive PII? Some transcriptions we've seen keep prefixes and it's worrying.
01:37 Jon Park: Quick clarification — the KV cache is per-session and we can enable prefix redaction; it's not written to disk unless you enable long-term cache. But fair point, we'll include config toggles in the runbook.
01:50 Lina Torres: For rollback criteria, we prefer hard thresholds: if p99 latency increases > 30% or error rate > 1% for 5 minutes, auto-cut back to previous routing. Does Redwood support an automatic rollback?
02:05 Jon Park: Yes, we have automated fallback policies; we can wire in your thresholds and trigger route switch within 60s. We'll also keep an alert channel in Ops.
02:15 Carlos Ruiz: About model variants — are you suggesting we use a quantized variant for cost or the full FP16 for quality? There's a risk in switching now.
02:24 Maya Patel: Good question. Our recommendation for the pilot is to use the production-quality variant you have in staging (FP16) and enable quantized (INT8) as an A/B after baseline is stable. That way we can measure cost savings without impacting initial quality metrics.
02:37 Aisha Khan: If we run A/B in the canary window, what's the easiest way to compare outputs? Do you produce diff reports or BLEU-style metrics?
02:46 Jon Park: We provide side-by-side samples and an automatic similarity score plus our eval pipeline that runs your prompt set and flags regressions by threshold. We'll share the reports to a staging dashboard (Grafana + our eval UI).
02:59 Serena Li: We'll also wire Redwood Alerts to your PagerDuty, and we can create a per-canary run dashboard template to reuse.
03:10 Ben Cho: Security question — for private deployment option, what's the SLA and who manages patching?
03:16 Maya Patel: For Private deployments there's a support add-on; we can do customer-managed Kubernetes where you control patches, or we can offer managed patching with stricter maintenance windows. We'll put options in the doc.
03:30 Carlos Ruiz: Timeline — we want the canary the week of Jan 20 if possible. We need to coordinate ops windows and have the runbook ahead of time.
03:37 Maya Patel: Sounds good. We'll aim to deliver the runbook by Jan 12. That includes pre-checklist, canary steps, monitoring playbook, rollback steps, and post-canary validation.
03:50 Aisha Khan: For monitoring, can you also include token-level cost breakdown per route? Our finance team wants a cost projection for 1M monthly tokens.
03:58 Jon Park: Yes, we can include token-level accounting and projected unit costs for dedicated vs hosted. We'll add a 'cost delta' table in the runbook.
04:08 Lina Torres: On the canary cutoff — do you support gradual ramping? e.g., 5% -> 10% -> 25% over several hours with checks at each step?
04:17 Jon Park: Absolutely, we have rollout policies that support staged increases with hold periods and automated metrics gating. We'll propose a ramp plan in the runbook.
04:28 Carlos Ruiz: Also want to ensure we have a human-in-the-loop hold — ops can pause or abort the ramp.
04:33 Maya Patel: We'll make sure the runbook includes manual pause steps and a single-click abort action in your routing control plane.
04:40 Ben Cho: On compliance, we'll need the SOC2 cert and ISO summary; you mentioned audit logs earlier, but also need proof of encryption at rest for any cached artifacts.
04:50 Maya Patel: We'll attach the SOC2 summary and an encryption at-rest whitepaper. For caching, we'll document retention settings and redaction options.
04:59 Lina Torres: Any blockers we should call out?
05:02 Carlos Ruiz: Main blockers are security sign-off (Ben) and our ability to allocate an ops window on Jan 20. Also need acceptance criteria signed by product.
05:12 Maya Patel: OK. We'll put these as dependencies in the runbook and also include a checklist for sign-offs.
05:18 Serena Li: One more operational note — during the canary we recommend a 2hr maintenance window to allow for observation and rollbacks, plus a 30-min warmup for KV caches.
05:29 Aisha Khan: For the staging load test — Jon, can you simulate the same burst patterns we see at peak? We have a spike of 400 RPS for 30s on Mondays.
05:38 Jon Park: Yep, we'll run a synthetic test that mirrors your QPS curve and capture autoscaler behavior.
05:45 Carlos Ruiz: Pricing question — what's the delta between dedicated reserved capacity and burst pricing during the canary?
05:52 Maya Patel: We'll send an updated pricing sheet; short answer: reserved gives lower unit cost but requires a commit. For pilots, customers often use a small dedicated pool plus burst to handle spikes. We'll include examples in the pricing doc.
06:05 Lina Torres: Let's recap next steps quickly.
06:08 Maya Patel: Recap: Redwood will share runbook + monitoring dashboard (Maya), SE will run staging load test (Jon), Nimbus will provide top routes and sign-off timeline (Aisha/Carlos), Ben will confirm security checklist. We'll target canary week of Jan 20.
06:25 Carlos Ruiz: Sounds good and thanks everyone.
06:28 Maya Patel: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the doc and schedule a 30-min dry run before Jan 20.
06:33 Meeting ends.
